summary: Bass River lighthouse, built 1907 on Cobequid Bay, Nova Scotia; deactivated in 1992, privately owned since 1994, closed to visitors.

light.characteristic: fixed red (1908 report; 1922 to 1941 per NSLPS); fixed white (1990 per NSLPS)

structures.note: Enclosed wooden building, square in plan, with a square wooden lantern, the whole painted white (1908 report). NSLPS gives 32 ft tower height. Moved about 1,000 ft in 1966 (NSLPS).

access.note: Privately owned since 1994. NSLPS asks visitors to take photos from the road. LF: grounds and tower closed.

facts.agency: private owner (sold out of Crown ownership in 1994)

events.note: Built by contract; the Department's report for the twelve months ending March 31, 1908 describes the finished light. LF and Colchester give 1907.
David Vance appointed first keeper, 24 October 1907, $100 a year (LF).
Moved about 1,000 ft; elevation raised from 39 to 41 ft (NSLPS).
NSLPS history item says 'automated by this date' with 1973. NSLPS's top summary says 'Automated by c. 1992'. The sources conflict (see notes).
NSLPS lists the characteristic as fixed white in 1990; earlier fixed red.
Colchester: deactivated 1992; LF: around 1992. NSLPS history gives discontinued 1991.
Went into private ownership from the Crown (Colchester); sold 1994 (LF).

keepers.name: David Vance
keepers.note: First keeper, appointed 24 October 1907 at $100 a year; salary $150 by 1924 (LF: 'through at least 1924'). Listed at Bass River in the Department's keeper statement printed 1912.

corrections.why: LF, Colchester and NSLPS all give 1907 as the year the light was built and lit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1907 for the tower agrees with LF, Colchester and NSLPS. The Department's report for the twelve months ending March 31, 1908 describes the completed light, which fits a 1907 build.
Record and Colchester give 1992; LF says around 1992; NSLPS's history gives 'discontinued' in 1991. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: The contractor's name is printed 'S. Beekwith' in the 1908 report (OCR reads it cleanly); Colchester's page and some other sources say Samuel Beckwith. Check the page image (scan p. 73, printed p. 64). The contract base price is not used: the OCR of it is garbled ('$4.")0'). The report gives the range as 7 miles; it is recorded here as 7 nautical miles by the guide's convention and should be checked. NSLPS conflicts within itself: automation '1973' in the history list against 'c. 1992' at the top, and discontinued 1991 against deactivated 1992 elsewhere. Light colour: fixed red in 1908 and 1922 to 1941 per NSLPS, fixed white in 1990 per NSLPS. Keeper table in the 1912 printed report: matched by the printed line 'Bass River : David Vance', so the match is by line, not column position; the year of the table (fiscal year) is not confirmed beyond 'printed 1912'. No women keepers or other keepers were found in the sources read. The Marine reports' 1918 to 1920 hits for 'Bass River' are shipbuilders and a wharfinger list, not the light, and are not used. No storms or wrecks tied to the station were found, so the chapter is omitted. LF's suggestion to view the light from the shoreline is not repeated: the property is private. The novascotiavacation.ca tourism page was not used (it gives different dates and is generated copy). Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1912 statement page image (scan p. 242, printed p. 235) was read. The Bass River row lines up David Vance with the station, so the match is by row position and is confirmed by the image; the same row's salary column appears to read 140 00, which fits neither LF's $100 (1907) nor $150 (1924), so the salary is not used in the story. The 1908 report page (scan p. 73, printed p. 64) is confirmed by the corpus page label. The story now gives the range as 7 miles, as printed, because the report does not say nautical miles; the facts field range_nm 7 should be checked against that before publication. The story's tower distance is now about 122 m (400 ft), the lantern is described as square and wooden, the site-change wording follows the report's old site, and the 1912 entry is no longer shown as a quotation of the printed layout.
